newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish police end Peruvian consulate occupation.
newsitem.headline: Danish police end Peruvian consulate occupation.

text.p: Danish police said on Monday they had ended a brief occupation of Peru's consulate-general by unarmed demonstrators protesting the death of Peruvian rebels in the storming of the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
"It was a peaceful action and at no point was there any drama or violence. The group was not armed and gave themselves up peacefully," a police spokesman told Reuters.

He said that police removed six demonstrators and a three-strong crew from cable TV station TV Stop, a community-based station traditionally sympathetic to local radical groups, from the consulate after a one-hour occupation.
"All nine are now under arrest and undergoing questioning," the spokesman added.

A local pressure group, the Committee for the Release of MRTA Prisoners in Peru, said the action was in sympathy with 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels who died when the Peruvian army ended the five-month Lima hostage drama with a raid last week.
All but one of the 72 hostages held by the MRTA were rescued alive in the raid but two Peruvian soldiers were killed.
During the Copenhagen sit-in the young Danish demonstrators hung out of the consulate-general's windows and shouted slogans, police said.
They called for an immediate inquiry into the Peruvian army action and demanded that the Danish government condemn it.

Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori has denied reports that some of the MRTA rebels holding the hostages were executed by Peruvian troops after being captured in the raid on the Japanese ambassador's residence.
"That is completely false. There were no executions," Fujimori told Reuters after the hostage drama had ended.
